source: Zenodo record 6974535, file DAN_Pixelization_Table_sol_3333.csv (DAN instrument team)
citation: Sergei Nikiforov, Maya Djachkova, Denis Lisov (2022). Water and chlorine in the Martian subsurface along the traverse of NASA's Curiosity rover: DAN measurement profiles along the traverse [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6974535
coverage_note: Landing to sol 3333 only (the table has no sol column; the limit is from the record's readme). The last pixel is at latitude -4.74984, 27155 m along a 38799 m track, so everything after that has no DAN value here. Chlorine exists only where the rover made an active (neutron-pulse) measurement.
notes: water_wt_pct is Water Equivalent Hydrogen (WEH) in weight percent: the amount of water that would hold the hydrogen DAN senses, whatever form the hydrogen is really in (the record says 'water ... content in shallow Martian subsurface'). cl_wt_pct is Absorption Equivalent Chlorine (AEC) in weight percent: the chlorine that would absorb as many thermal neutrons as the ground does. The errors are the statistical errors given per pixel. The source has two pixel types on a 0.00005 degree (about 3 m) grid: PAD, from active measurements with the pulsed 14 MeV neutron generator (method: Lisov et al. 2018, Astronomy Letters 44, 482, doi:10.1134/S1063773718070034), which carry both WEH and AEC; and PPD, from passive neutron-background counts while roving, converted to WEH by the 'Method of Referencing by Active Data' (Nikiforov et al. 2020, Icarus 346, 113818, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2020.113818), which carry WEH only. Neither the readme nor the record states a sensing depth or a layering model for these numbers; each is a single bulk value per pixel. For depth, the PDS DAN data product specification (depth_reference_url, section 2.1) describes the instrument as sensing hydrogen-bearing material 'in a shallow layer (~1 m) of Mars' subsurface' and lists 'the upper <0.5 m' as the layer whose structure it investigates. That is a statement about the instrument, not a property recorded in this table.
thinning_note: Each source pixel was snapped to the nearest vertex of the route in data/site.json to get chain_m. Pixels whose vertex falls in the same 5 m stretch of track were averaged into one point: lat, lon, chain_m, water and its error are plain means over the n_pixels pixels (active and passive together); cl and its error are means over the n_active active pixels, null where there is none; the member is the most common one. water_err is the mean of the source errors, not an error of the mean. Where n_pixels is 1 the values are the source values unchanged.
source_readme:
DAN_Pixel_Map_sol_3333.jpg
Water map as derived from the DAN instrument data from a landing site up to MSL sol 3333. 
Pixels of Passive Data (PPD) are presented as squares, Pixels with Active Data (PAD) are presented as circles.

DAN_Pixelization_Table_sol_3333.csv
File contains 7 columns, each row representing one pixel:
	(1) - the successive number of pixel
	(2) - a mark of pixel type, either Pixel with Active Data (PAD) or Pixel of Passive Data (PPD)
	(3) - longitude coordinates  of the center of the pixel
	(4) - latitude coordinates of the center of the pixel
	(5) - the associated member of the MSL stratigraphic column
	(6) - estimated WEH value (wt.%) in PAD or PPD
	(7) - estimated AEC value (wt.%) in PAD
